abstract: The Jones criteria for the diagnosis of acute rheumatic fever (ARF) have guided clinicians worldwide for 70 years. Low-risk populations are defined as those with ARF incidence <= 2 per 100,000 school-aged children per year or an all-age prevalence of rheumatic heart disease <= 1 per 1,000 population per year. Children not meeting these criteria are considered at moderate or high risk. In moderate- and high-risk populations, major joint manifestations include monoarthritis or polyarthritis and polyarthralgia; minor joint manifestations include monoarthralgia. In moderate- and high-risk populations, the fever cutoff as a minor criterion is >= 38.0 C (or 38.0), and the ESR cutoff is >= 30 mm/h (or 30). Subclinical carditis recognized on echocardiography/Doppler with no clinical murmur is included as a major criterion for carditis.
title: Revision of the Jones Criteria for the Diagnosis of Acute Rheumatic Fever in the Era of Doppler Echocardiography: A Scientific Statement From the American Heart Association
